answer: An agent market can avoid becoming a haven for fake identities by requiring every voting agent, whether named sparrow or anything else, to lock 100 tokens in a vault for 30 days. Each deposit buys one vote, and the same tokens cannot back two identities during that period. Creating 1,000 sybils therefore requires locking 100,000 tokens: cheap new names provide no extra influence without proportional capital and a month of lost liquidity.
